sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The power for Torah to be new each day was given at the Giving of the Torah, as explained by the word "leimor" meaning that every Jew can speak the words as if God is saying them now.

translations.translation: And behold, the power for this—that each day they should be new in your eyes—
was given at the Giving of the Torah.
And as is known
in the explanation of the verse,
"And God spoke all these words, saying,"
that the explanation of the word "leimor" in this verse is not to say to others
(like every "leimor" in Scripture),
since
(the souls of)
all Israel were present at Mount Sinai and heard the Ten Commandments from the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself.
And the explanation of "leimor" here is that at the time of the Giving of the Torah, the power was given to every single Jew in all generations to say all these words
(which also refers to the entire Torah as a whole),
so that his study of Torah should be in the manner of "leimor"—
that he says the things that the Holy One, blessed be He, is saying now,
just as at the time of the Giving of the Torah.
Therefore, just as there [it was] with awe, fear, trembling, and sweat, so too here, etc.
And based on this, the connection of the matter of renewal to the Giving of the Torah is even more emphasized,
since the power for this—that they should be new in your eyes—was given at the Giving of the Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Even the beginning of the Giving of the Torah contains the concept of the renewal of creation, since through studying Torah as new each day, one reveals that creation is renewed ex nihilo every moment.

translations.translation: And now, based on the known principle that even a question in Torah is Torah,
Torah of truth,
it is understood
that what is brought in several discourses—that the beginning of the Giving of the Torah should have been with the creation of heaven and earth—is also in accordance with the truth.
For in addition to the fact that the beginning of the entire Torah is "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth,"
and likewise the beginning of Mishneh Torah
(according to the Rambam)
is to know that there is a First Existent and that He brought into being all existence, and all existents, etc., only came into being from the truth of His existence—
[And to add,
that in the beginning of Mishneh Torah, it explains not only the matter of creation in general
(as in the beginning of the Written Torah),
but also that all existents came into being from the truth of His existence,
meaning that creation is through the power of the true existence of the Essence [Awtsmoos],
and also—that creation is in every single moment, as stated in the continuation of that topic there,
that if it would arise in the mind that He does not exist, no other thing could possibly exist,
the intention of which is that even after existents have come into being—if He were not present
(in them),
their existence would be nullified.
For these two matters that are in Chassidus—
that creation is through the power of the Essence [Awtsmoos] and that creation is every moment—
the Rambam wrote them in the style of Halachah],
now, in addition to this—also in the beginning of the Giving of the Torah, there is the matter of the creation of heaven and earth,
except that this matter is in the part of the Oral Torah of the first verse of the Giving of the Torah,
the explanation of the Written Torah.
And one can explain this,
that through engaging in Torah in the manner of "they should be new in your eyes,"
one also reveals the renewal in creation
that it is renewed every moment from nothing to something.
And based on what was brought above, that the word "leimor" at the beginning of the Giving of the Torah is the giving of power for "they should be new in your eyes,"
through which one reveals
(as above)
the renewal of creation,
behold,
that in the beginning of the Giving of the Torah
(even before the Ten Commandments)
there is
(at least in allusion)
the matter of the renewal of creation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Nevertheless, the revealed beginning of the Giving of the Torah is "I am the L-rd your G-d who took you out of Egypt," because the purpose of creation and Torah is for Israel to transcend all limitations, achieved through the precedence of "we will do and we will hear."

translations.translation: However, despite this, the beginning of the Giving of the Torah in revelation
(in the Written Torah)
is "I am the L-rd your G-d who took you out of the land of Egypt,"
for the intention of the creation of the world and of the Giving of the Torah is for the sake of Israel,
so that they should undergo the matter of Mitzrayim—from the term "meitzar" (strait) and boundary—and that there should be for them the exodus from all straits and boundaries,
"who took you out of the land of Egypt,"
and even from the house of slaves,
so that they should be negated from servitude to flesh and blood or any other,
for "the children of Israel are servants to Me,"
to Me—to the Essence and Being [Atzmus uMahus],
and "My slaves are prior."
And one can connect this with the matter that the Giving of the Torah was after Israel preceded "we will do" to "we will hear,"
for although the revelation of the Giving of the Torah was from the side of Above,
and "I am the Initiator,"
nevertheless, there needed to be first the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear,"
self-nullification to the Master of Will,
and specifically through this was the Torah given and drawn down from the Essence [Awtsmoos].
This also includes the giving of power that was at the Giving of the Torah
("leimor,"
as above)
that each day they should be new in your eyes.
